previousItemsStillOpen: r1 photo 1 / artifact 2, reentry (was blocker, now major): the pinwheel, the hose and the hairline are gone, the capsule is lit and the wake narrows; but from the side the shock layer is a smooth airbrushed clipped lobe, from the front a featureless white ellipse with a pencil-tip wake behind it, from behind a pink-white ring round a dark disc, and in the integration lab by day (dev/i4-reentry.png) a flat pink-white lens with no streaming structure

r1 photo 2 / artifact 8, splash (was blocker, still blocker for the photo lens): foam is lace now and drops are streaked, but the crown is a soft blurred bowl covered with identical white pills, and a ring of cotton-wool puffs hangs round the capsule from +1.8 s to +5 s; the water itself never moves

r1 photo 3 / artifact 9 and 22, explosion (was blocker, now major/minor): glitter, rods and the square secondary are gone and the soot phase is good; the fire at 0.2-0.6 s is a soft pastel ball with no dark folds, fragment trails are straight pale pins with a dot, the night ball at 1.5 s is one sepia tone, and the dark bar on a fragment trail in close-2.5s is still there

r1 photo 7 / artifact 17 and 18, staging and vacuum ignition (major): the orange sunburst is gone; the retro and ullage jets are still soft cream searchlight cones and the hydrolox ignition is a soft round blue-white ball three stage diameters across

r1 photo 8 / artifact 6 and 20, pad cloud (major): whiter and with shaded billows in the lab, but still a low soft mound resolved at a quarter of the resolution; in the game it is a set of grey out-of-focus blobs with detached round puffs; small dark wormy scribbles remain (liftoff-chase/t6-day), and the view from inside is still a flat orange-tan fill

r1 photo 9 / artifact 15, solid motors (major): the edge is firmer at sea level, but the smoke is still cream, lit evenly and without a shaded side; at 30 km, 60 km and in vacuum the cones are still sand-grained spotlights with worm-textured fans and jagged tips

r1 photo 10 (reefed part) / artifact 12, canopies (major): full canopies are fixed; reef-1 mains are still ribbed peanut-shaped bulbs with dark creases, and at reef 2 the third canopy still sits inside the mouth of the upper right one

r1 photo 11 / artifact 11, cut-away canopies (major): no longer sausages with rain, now half-inflated bulbs that hang in the air for six seconds with their lines gathered to a point below them (jellyfish)

r1 photo 12 / artifact 13 and 19, lunar dust (was major, now blocker in a new form): the painted sunburst and the dashes in the sky are gone, but the sheet now glows as a haze band 8-9 degrees high ABOVE the horizon, and in the integration lab it greys out the whole frame; the lander's legs at night are still clipped white lines beside a dark body
r1 photo 15 / artifact 14, RCS (major): firings are visible now in sun and shadow and light the hull with a gradient, but each is a soft round glow blob with no jet shape

r1 artifact 3, exposure (was major, now minor): the lift-off sequence still steps about half a stop when the cloud leaves the frame (chase sky 60,74,95 at T+0..6 against 73,87,110 at T+10; pad camera 70,85,109 against 83,98,123), and the deterministic and live shots of engine-atlas-9m/sl-full still differ by about 0.6 EV (sky 91 against 110)

r1 artifact 4, grain of half-resolution volumes (was major, now major only for the low-pressure solid-motor fans; minor elsewhere): the denoise pass removed most stipple; sand grain and worm texture remain in engine-solids at 30 km, 60 km and vacuum, and the translucent near field at the booster nozzles is marbled

r1 artifact 5, surfaces lit as by a point (was major, partly open): hull and bells are fixed; the capsule's heat-shield face next to the solid motors is still a flat clipped white ellipse, the booster's base plate is a flat cream disc, and the lunar legs at night are neon lines
r1 photo 14 / artifact 10 (part), trails (minor now): the night reentry trail is fixed; the ascent trail in haze (haze-trail-50km.png) is still a uniform soft stick with a hard lower end
r1 photo 18 / artifact 16, canopy shadows on the sea: unchanged near-black blobs on the lab's Lambert sea; still not checked on the real ocean

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/impact-0.4s.png, impact-1s.png, impact-1.8s.png, impact-2.5s.png, impact-5s.png, close-0.4s.png, close-0.4s-live.png, close-1s.png, cut-away-1s.png
findings.defect: The splash still reads as a particle effect at a glance. At +0.4 s and +1 s the crown is a soft, blurred white bowl with no sheets, ligaments or fingers, and it is covered with fat white pills of nearly one size (close-0.4s-live: rice-grain shapes about 4 x 8 px, hard-edged, evenly scattered). At +1.8 s and +2.5 s the capsule sits in a ring of out-of-focus cotton-wool puffs a capsule height tall; at +5 s wisps of the same white vapour still hang over the foam. It looks like smoke or steam round the capsule, not water. The sea surface itself is untouched in every frame: no cavity, no ring wave, no collapse column.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/apollo17-splashdown.jpg and dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg (the sea round a capsule is dark, glossy water with crisp foam; nothing hangs in the air). Apollo, Orion and Dragon splashdown film: a lumpy translucent wall of water one to two capsule heights high that tears into ragged curtains and chunky spray of very different sizes and has fallen back within 1.5 s, leaving a boiling pale patch and expanding ring waves. heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg: thrown water is crisp, streaky sheets with a bright sunlit edge, never a soft cloud.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/splash.ts: the crown is marched as a volume in the half-resolution image and comes out soft; the 'mist' body (MIST_LIFE = 3 flight times, mistH up to 0.38 of the peak, ring noise) is kept for seconds. data/defs/visuals/plumes.json particles.spray: mistCount 160 sprites of 0.6-2.2 m that live 1.2-3.4 s are the cotton puffs; the 1800 drops are drawn as streaks 3.5 x their shutter path with a narrow visible size range, lit uniformly white. Nothing displaces the ocean.
findings.fixDirection: Remove the long-lived mist sprites (or cut their size to under 0.3 m, opacity to a few per cent and life to under 0.8 s) and end the mist body within one flight time. Build the crown from a thickness field with strong azimuthal breaks (fingers, gaps, a lean along the horizontal entry speed) and render its dense part sharp (full resolution or a mesh sheet with refraction and a bright rim), keeping the volume only for the fine spray at its top. Give drops a heavy-tailed size distribution (a few large blobs, many sub-pixel ones drawn as energy-conserving smudges) with sun glints instead of flat white. File the request with the ocean package for a cavity, a collapse column and ring waves at the entry point, and shoot the sequence on the real ocean.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/lunar/30m-day.png, 30m-day-close.png, 10m-day.png, 10m-day-live.png, 5m-day-close.png, 5m-day-close-live.png, perf-lunar-descent-with-dust.png; out/screens/vfx/dev/i4-lunar-hover.png (integration lab, taken 5 minutes before the last dust commit 84b6f11)
findings.defect: The Moon has an atmosphere. In every sunlit lunar frame, already at 30 m, a grey glow rises from the horizon into the black sky: in lunar/30m-day the sky column at x=200 goes 118 at the horizon, 58 forty pixels up, 20 eighty pixels up, and reaches black only 140 px (about 8-9 degrees) above it. With the real lander and terrain at an 8 m hover (dev/i4-lunar-hover.png) the whole frame is a grey fog: frame median (112,110,122), no pixel darker than 5, no terrain and no horizon visible, the sky grey to the top edge, with lens flares floating in it. On the ground itself the lab frames show only faint radial rays under the lander and one dark streaked wedge (5m-day-close, x 1040-1280, y 530-600) with a stippled edge.
findings.realReference: Apollo 11-17 descent film from the LM window and Blue Ghost / Chang'e landing video: the sky stays black down to a sharp horizon; the dust is a thin, fast sheet hugging the surface at 1-3 degrees, visible as bright streaks racing outward that wash out rocks and craters UNDER the horizon; the lander's shadow falls on it crisply. out/qa/ref/moon-surface/mount-hadley.jpg and lm-falcon-lrv.jpg: black sky directly above sunlit ground, no haze of any height.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/dust.ts: the sheet's vertical profile is exponential with scale height H = max(r, r0) * tanE (line 119), so 300 m out it is some 20 m thick with an endless tail above; amount falls only as (r0/r)^0.7 out to sheetMinReach 320 m (plumes.json particles.dust: sheetDepth 1.4, sheetReachRadii 80). A level or rising line of sight therefore passes through hundreds of metres of sunlit dust above the camera. The round's own note says the i4 frame was a white-out and only the forward-scattering share was halved afterwards (phase mix 0.7 -> 0.45), which cannot bring the terrain back.
findings.fixDirection: Bound the sheet above by the ejection cone: no dust above the highest launch elevation (2-3 degrees from the foot of the jet), with a short smooth top instead of an exponential tail, so that nothing can scatter above the horizon for a camera higher than a couple of metres. Let the density fall at least as 1/r^2 beyond a few nozzle heights and cap the optical depth along any ray at about 0.6, so the sheet veils the ground and softens the foot of the horizon by a degree at most. Put the brightness into fine radial streaks that move, not into a uniform haze. Add a spec in the integration lab: at an 8 m hover the sky 5 degrees above the horizon stays under 2 % of white and at least half of the terrain pixels keep their local contrast; re-shoot dev/i4-lunar-hover.png.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/liftoff/t10-night.png, liftoff/t10-day.png (x 608-752, y 338-339); liftoff-chase/t6-day-live.png and t6-day.png (cloud top at x 780-880, y 290); for comparison liftoff-probe/pad-night-T6.png
findings.defect: The pad cloud is cut off along a ruler-straight horizontal line. In liftoff/t10-night the cloud's top is a flat edge 144 px wide against the black sky with the flame standing on it like a candle on a table: in every column from x=608 to x=744 the luminance jumps by 29 to 76 levels between y=338 and y=339 (at x=690: 28, 81, 162 on three successive rows), far sharper than a quarter-resolution volume can be. The row is exactly the lab's horizon (liftoff/t10-day at x=100: sky to ground between y=338 and 339), and only a faint 4 px leak of cloud shows above it. Four seconds earlier from the same camera (liftoff-probe/pad-night-T6) the cloud top is lower and naturally lumpy. In the chase frames the far right part of the cloud also ends flat on the horizon line while the part next to the vehicle rises above it.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis1-launch-1.jpg, artemis2-launch-2.jpg, atlasv-oa6-liftoff.jpg: an exhaust cloud has a lumpy cauliflower outline against the sky on every side; no part of it ends on a straight line, and it does not change where the background changes from ground to sky.
findings.likelyCause: Not confirmed; the edge is one pixel sharp and sits on the sky/ground depth step, so it is made where full-resolution or half-resolution scene depth enters. Candidates: (1) src/render/vfx/smoke.ts COMBINE_WGSL (lines 501-562): the pixel's z is clamped to 1e7 and each ray is weighted by 1 / (1 + (12 diff)^2) against its two cut depths; rays of sky pixels beside rays that end on the far ground, or the 'best ray' fallback, may drop the smoke while keeping the emitters (the flame is intact above the line). (2) the per-sample atmosphere (vfxAtmosphere -> applyAtmosphere in src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts 695-708), whose cloud-span term (clouds.depth / clouds.screen) and aerial slices are read per pixel and act with distance (the cut is total from 430 m, partial from 150 m). (3) the cylinder that bounds the march (smoke.ts 319-331, height from line 875) if the lab's pad camera happens to sit at its top.
findings.fixDirection: Discriminate first: re-shoot liftoff/t10 with the pad camera 20 m higher and 20 m lower. If the cut follows the horizon it is screen-space: then shoot with options.skipAtmosphere, and with the depth weight in COMBINE_WGSL forced to 1, to find which term removes smoke over sky pixels; make sky pixels take the same rays as their ground neighbours when the smoke lies in front of both. If the cut stays at a world height, bound the march by the cells the cloud has actually reached (the simulated cell box) plus a margin, and fade density towards any bound so that no bound can show as an edge. Add a spec on liftoff/t10-night: along the cloud's upper outline no row holds more than 40 consecutive columns whose largest one-pixel luminance step lies on the same row.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/reentry-views/side-close-1.0.png, side-close-1.0-live.png, side-close-0.3.png, front-1.0.png, front-1.0-live.png, front-0.3.png, behind-1.0.png, behind-0.3.png; reentry/plasma-1.0-day.png, plasma-1.0-night.png; perf-reentry.png; dev/i4-reentry.png, dev/i4-reentry-fu4.png
findings.defect: The plasma is an airbrushed glow, not streaming gas. From the side the shock layer is a smooth clipped white lobe with a soft pink halo and no internal structure; the streamers on the back shell are soft parallel stripes like a pleated lampshade. From the front it is a featureless clipped white ellipse with one faint inner ring, and the wake behind it ends in a grey pencil point with a bright dot. From behind it is a pink-white ring round a dark disc (a solar eclipse), with a red-brown smear at lower left in behind-1.0 and no gas streaming towards the camera. In the integration lab over a sunlit Earth (dev/i4-reentry.png) it is a flat pink-white lens standing off the heat shield, wider than the shield, with a barely visible wake; the hull behind it is clean white with no orange on the shoulder, and no ablation sparks are visible.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/eft1-plasma-side-window.jpg: a dense field of fine, irregular streaks of very different brightness, pink-magenta to salmon with a white-yellow core, nothing smooth anywhere. progress42-reentry.jpg, atv3-reentry.jpg and dragon-reentry-from-iss.jpg: a compact clipped head and a thin trail (this part the 50 km frames now match). Hayabusa and Orion tracking film: the glow wraps the shoulder, flickers, and sheds sparks into a turbulent wake.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plasma.ts: the layer is a Gaussian fall-off round the stagnation point with one smooth colour ramp, scaled three stops over white so its body clips, and its glare (bloom) supplies the rest; the streamer noise is low-contrast and band-limited by the half-resolution march at this distance, so it averages out. BASE_GLOW fills the wake evenly. Sparks (particles.ablation: rate 450, life 0.15-0.5 s, 1.2-4 cm) are too small and short-lived to show. By day the layer's luminance sits near the sunlit hull, so it reads as fog.
findings.fixDirection: Put structure in at the scale the march can hold: a thin bright bow-shock sheet at the standoff (brightest at its edge-on rim, not a filled lobe) and, behind the shoulder, streamers with at least 4:1 contrast at two scales that flicker along the flow; drive them with noise advected at flow speed so that live frames differ. Grade the gas by temperature (white-yellow at the stagnation point, magenta-pink in the layer, orange in the wake) instead of one clipped white. From behind, fill the base with converging, streaking gas brighter than the back shell so there is no dark disc in a ring. Make the shoulder and back shell glow orange with heat. Emit fewer, larger, longer-lived ablation sparks that curve into the wake. Check the day case at the game's exposure: the stagnation region must still clip.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/dev/a4-liftoff-t1.png, a4-liftoff-t3.png, a4-liftoff-t6.png, a4-liftoff-t10.png (the real game); out/screens/vfx/liftoff/t10-day.png, liftoff-chase/t6-day.png, perf-lift-off-from-a-chase-camera-at-150-m.png
findings.defect: In the game the pad cloud is the weakest thing in the frame. At T+1 it is a handful of grey, out-of-focus blobs gathered round the lower third of the vehicle, with four detached round puffs lying on the apron like cotton balls; the flame trench in front of the mount is empty and nothing is blown out of it. At T+6 the cloud is wispy cream ribbons and soft lumps beside a pin-sharp tower; at T+10 it is a flat grey dome (median 165,158,152, darker than the cumulus in the sky and no brighter than the white hull) with almost no billow detail. It rises round the hull instead of being driven away from it, stays under a quarter of the vehicle's height, and is tan-beige in the chase views.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis2-launch-2.jpg: brilliant white steam, the brightest object in the frame, shot sideways out of the trench in two hard-edged cauliflower masses as wide as the pad, with crisp towers in front. apollo4-liftoff.jpg: tan exhaust with brown shadow sides billowing sideways and upward, larger than the vehicle. sts134-ssme-ignition.jpg: steam rolling out low from under the platform, never wrapping the stack.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: the cloud is marched at a quarter of the resolution and upsampled with a cubic B-spline (soft everywhere); the source is 'where the jet meets the pad' with a weak trench focus (trenchFocus scaled down with nozzle height), so the gas spreads as a ring round the mount; padSmoke yields and jet momentum keep it small; the detached puffs are separate soft particles or isolated cells. In the game's daylight exposure the steam's albedo and the sun term leave it at mid-grey.
findings.fixDirection: Drive the first seconds from the trench: emit the steam and exhaust at the trench exits with the jet's momentum (two opposed horizontal jets that then rise), and keep the space round the hull clear until the vehicle has left. Raise yield and speed so the cloud is pad-sized by T+6 and taller than a third of the vehicle by T+10. Make sunlit steam the brightest diffuse thing in the frame (albedo near 1, multiple-scattering floor) with exhaust-tinted tan only near the flame. Spend resolution where it shows: half resolution for the march within a few hundred metres, or a sharpening detail pass on the silhouette, so that its edge is as crisp as the tower beside it. Remove the isolated puff sprites.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/dev/a4-liftoff-t6.png, a4-liftoff-t10.png; out/screens/vfx/plumes-close/booster-45m.png, booster-45m-night.png, booster-110m.png; liftoff-chase/t10-day.png; liftoff/t10-day.png; engine-atlas-9m/sl-full.png, sl-min.png, 10km-min.png, sl-full-live.png
findings.defect: The booster flame now clips (62 % of the jet patch in booster-45m at 250 or more), which removes the round-1 complaint, but its shape gives it away. In the game it is a plain white stick with a thin orange rim, narrower than the vehicle, of the same width and brightness from the nozzles to the cloud. In the lab it is an airbrushed column whose edge is a smooth orange gradient, and from T+10 it bulges and necks every two to three diameters like a twisted rope or a candle flame. In the engine tiles the clipped part is a flat white cut-out with a scalloped outline lying in a tan haze, with a second detached island of flame downstream (engine-atlas-9m/sl-full x 885-1040, sl-min, 10km-min). No Mach discs are visible in any frame, and at night the flame has no glare beyond its own soft edge.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/apollo4-liftoff.jpg and artemis2-launch-1.jpg: the flame leaves the nozzles straight-sided and streaked along the flow, as wide as the vehicle, widens steadily and breaks into fine turbulence at its edge, turning yellow-orange and then smoky; it is several vehicle diameters long with no periodic bulges. sts51f-ignition.jpg: a hard, ragged, brilliant edge. artemis1-launch-1.jpg and atlasv-oa6-liftoff.jpg: at night a wide glare surrounds the flame and lights the air.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts and data/defs/visuals/plumes.json plume.methalox-booster: one low-frequency displacement of the boundary (noise.scaleRe, amount) makes the varicose wobble; the flame ends on a threshold of the same noise ('a flame with an edge' between 0.66 and 1.1 of its radius), which cuts islands off; afterburn.luminance 2.8e6 clips the whole cross-section so the diamonds (gain 32) and all internal structure vanish; bloom receives a soft-edged source and stays narrow.
findings.fixDirection: Keep the first two to three diameters straight and streaked, then widen the jet with the mixing layer (the merged nine-engine radius) rather than keep a column. Replace the single wobble with fine edge turbulence that grows downstream (two octaves at 0.2 and 0.6 of the local radius, advected at jet speed). Let luminance fall along the axis by a stop or two so the far flame is yellow-orange with visible eddies and the diamonds show in the first cells. Fade the flame out through soot-orange instead of ending it on a threshold, so no detached islands form. Feed a tight clipped core to bloom and add a wide low-level glare term at night.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/cut-away-1s.png, cut-away-6s.png, impact-5s.png; perf-chutes-and-splash.png
findings.defect: The released mains read as jellyfish. One second and six seconds after cut-away two half-inflated ribbed bulbs still float two to three capsule heights above the water, upright, having sunk about 30 m in five seconds; under each, all the lines hang in a smooth bundle gathered to a single point in mid-air with nothing on it. In impact-5s fans of straight lines enter from the top of the frame with no canopy visible.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/apollo9-floats.jpg: spent canopies lie flat on the water as bright limp sheets. apollo17-splashdown.jpg and dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg: a canopy still in the air after release has lost its shape, leans and streams sideways with the wind, its lines slack and trailing. Orion recovery film: the mains deflate within a second or two and settle on the sea beside the capsule.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/chutes.ts / canopyModel.ts drift state: inflation falls only to 0.3 of what it was and the axis stays near vertical (tips by at most 37 degrees) while the canopy sinks at cutDrift.sinkSpeed 6.5 m/s; the slack lines are 8-segment curves that all end at the old confluence point, which is kept as a rigid point under the canopy.
findings.fixDirection: After release let the crown collapse first: inflation to under 0.1 within about 1.5 s with strong random folds per gore, the canopy laid over on its side and carried downwind, falling at 8-12 m/s until it reaches the water and spreads flat. Release the confluence: the riser end falls ballistically, the lines trail as loose curves of unequal length above and behind the cloth, and fade under water. Shoot the sequence at +1, +3 and +6 s on the real ocean.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/chutes/mains-reef1-backlit.png, mains-reef2-backlit.png, drogues-reefed.png
findings.defect: Reefed mains are striped gourds. At reef 1 each canopy is a closed peanut-shaped bulb with hard dark creases between orange and grey stripes, a faint grid of white dashes over it and a ragged hem; at reef 2 they are ribbed onions, and the third canopy sits with its crown inside the mouth of the upper right one, so that the upper skirt band is drawn across the lower canopy like a belt (mains-reef2-backlit, x 640-760, y 150-200). Against the light all of them are lit like front-lit cloth: no glow through the fabric, no darker silhouette.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/artemis2-mains.jpg and demo1-four-mains.jpg: canopies of a cluster press against each other and never overlap; the cloth is smooth with fine ring slots and a scalloped hem. Orion CPAS reefing film: a first-stage reefed main is a long fluted tube with an open, fluttering mouth held by the reefing line and a small bulb at the crown; against the sun the cloth glows and the folds are soft shadows, not black lines.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/canopyModel.ts: the reefed profile closes the skirt to a bulb and the pleats (0.2 x slack) are deep enough to self-shadow into black creases at the mesh's gore resolution; the cluster angle spaces canopies by the full-open geometry, so partly open ones overlap, and there is no contact pass. chutes.ts lights both faces alike with little transmission at low inflation.
findings.fixDirection: Model reef 1 as an open-mouthed fluted tube (skirt circumference fixed by the reefing line, cloth above it bellying out a little, crown bulb small) and reef 2 as a wider one; soften the pleat shading and filter it with distance. Space the canopies of a cluster by their current maximum radius plus flutter and push touching sides flat. Give the cloth single-layer transmission against the sun at every inflation.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/engine-solids/sl-les.png, sl-les-live.png, sl-les-close-live.png, sl-retro.png, 10km-les.png, 10km-retro.png
findings.defect: Solid-motor exhaust is a soft cream-yellow cloud, lit evenly from every side, with a blurred lumpy outline; the white-hot root runs into it without a flame of its own colour. The four retro jets are soft cream fingers ending in clipped white dots. It looks like warm fog under a spotlight rather than dense smoke.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/sts51f-ignition.jpg: solid-rocket plumes are blinding white with a hard, torn edge. artemis2-launch-1.jpg: the smoke that follows is dense, opaque, white to grey with a clearly lit side and a shaded side and cauliflower billows. Pad Abort 1 film: a long clipped orange-white flame from each abort nozzle, then a grey-white trail with strong self-shadow.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts jetSample: the smoke takes one unshadowed sun term plus the plume's own glow (glowColor, glowLengthRe), so it is tinted cream along its whole length; the boundary is displaced by large scales only and the march is at half resolution.
findings.fixDirection: Add a short shadow march (two or three steps toward the sun, or an analytic depth along the sun direction) so the far side falls to grey; confine the glow to the first few exit diameters; give the smoke an albedo near white with billows at the scale of the local radius that sharpen downstream; keep a distinct clipped flame core two to four diameters long.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/engine-solids/30km-les.png, 30km-retro.png, 60km-les.png, 60km-retro.png, vac-les.png, vac-retro.png
findings.defect: At low pressure the solid-motor plumes are spotlight beams with rendering noise in plain view: a sand-grain stipple along the whole rim of each cone (30km-les), a vermicelli pattern of small swirls filling the fans (vac-retro, 3x crop at x 560-1000, y 180-460), and jagged, blocky tips with single bright pixels at the nozzles. With the flat white capsule base beside it, 30km-les reads as a lamp throwing a beam.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/falcon9-twilight-plume.jpg and soyuz-ms13-jellyfish.jpg: gas expanding at altitude is perfectly smooth at pixel scale, with soft large-scale structure only. Saturn V staging film: retro and ullage motors in near-vacuum are short bright streaks with a thin, quickly fading haze.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts: in the far field the particulate fan keeps the turbulence noise of the dense regime (the swirls are the noise texture seen at low density), sampled with one jittered offset per half-resolution pixel over a march whose bound was just tightened (plumeModel.ts jetShape, commit 1b283b9); the 3 x 3 denoise in volumes.ts cannot remove structure of that size, and the nozzle tips are under-sampled where the cone is narrower than a half-resolution pixel.
findings.fixDirection: Fade the turbulence amplitude to zero with falling pressure (a free expansion is laminar) and replace it by the smooth cos^n fan with faint striation already used for the liquid engines; lower the fan's scatter by about a stop; start the march inside the nozzle with a minimum of four samples across the tip or draw the first exit diameters analytically. Verify with the Laplacian standard deviation of a fan patch (target under 2 of 255).

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/engine-solids/sl-les.png, 10km-les.png, 30km-les.png, 60km-les.png, vac-les.png (heat-shield face at x 285-320, y 315-420); plumes-close/booster-45m.png and booster-45m-live.png (base plate); lunar/30m-night.png (legs, top cap)
findings.defect: Surfaces beside a flame are still flat, clipped shapes. The capsule's heat-shield face next to the abort motors is a uniform white ellipse in every solid-motor tile (sl-les: 90 % of the patch at 250 or more; vac-les 85 %), although it faces away from the motors. The booster's base plate is a flat cream disc with no gradient round the bells, and the pod exits are flat cream ellipses. The lunar lander at night has a dark body with three legs drawn as clipped white neon tubes, glowing footpads and a clipped white rectangle on its top cap.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/sts51f-ignition.jpg: hardware beside a plume is lit warm with smooth gradients and visible form. atlasv-oa6-liftoff.jpg: the aft end is rimmed by a broad falling gradient. out/qa/ref/moon-surface/lm-falcon-lrv.jpg: landing legs are matte struts whose brightness follows their orientation.
findings.likelyCause: The plume lights have a source radius since request vfx-5, but the light of a jet is still placed on its axis with the full intensity of the jet: a surface within a radius or two (the capsule base behind the tower motors, thin struts next to the lander's jet, the plate between the bells) receives it without the jet's own occlusion or a cosine to the visible flame. The top cap rectangle may be a lamp or emissive part of the lab model.
findings.fixDirection: Treat the jet as a line or capsule light whose near part is occluded by the vehicle (no light from the segment a surface cannot see), clamp per-surface illuminance to that of a hemisphere filled with the flame's luminance, and start the lit segment a few exit radii downstream. Verify three patches: the capsule base in sl-les is not clipped, the base plate in booster-45m shows a gradient of at least 30 levels, and the lunar legs at 30 m by night are under 200 with shading along their length.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/rcs/pulse-sun.png, all-sun.png, all-sun-12m.png, all-sun-12m-live.png, pulse-shadow.png, all-shadow.png, all-shadow-12m.png, all-shadow-12m-live.png
findings.defect: Thruster firings are now visible and light the hull with a gradient, but each is a soft round glow blob sitting on the port, with no direction, no core and no edge: from 12 m three pale smudges about 60 px across, the same in sun and shadow. A player cannot tell which way a thruster fires.
findings.realReference: Shuttle, Apollo and Dragon thruster firings: a sharp bright flash at the nozzle and a short, wide, faint cone that is clearly directed away from the port for one to two metres and is gone with the pulse; in shadow the cone itself is almost invisible and the flash lights nearby structure.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json plume.rcs: core luminance 400,000 with vacuumLengthRe 18, vacuumCoreRe 6 and vacuumGain 0.22 gives a short bright stub that is smaller than the bloom kernel, so bloom turns it into a ball; the march bound for smoky jets in vacuum was tightened again in the last commit (1b283b9), which also holds the puff.
findings.fixDirection: Shape before brightness: a cone of 20-30 degrees half-angle whose brightness falls as 1/x^2 over 1-2 m, with a core two to three exit diameters long that stays under the bloom threshold except in its first diameter; a faint sunlit scatter term for the cone in sunlight only; a sharp on/off envelope. Check from 12 m that the luminance profile along the thrust axis is at least three times longer than across it.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/explosion/day-0.2s.png, day-0.6s.png, close-0.6s.png, close-0.6s-live.png, day-1.5s.png, day-3.5s.png, night-1.5s.png, close-night-0.6s.png
findings.defect: The fireball is no longer glitter, but its fire phase is weak: at 0.2-0.6 s it is a soft cream-yellow ball (close-0.6s: median 249,229,182 inside the ball; no pixel reaches white in day-0.2s, day-0.6s or close-0.6s) of wispy pale folds with no dark soot wrapping bright cracks and no clipped core after the first flash. From 1.5 s the fragments are thin, pale, ruler-straight lines ending in a round dot, like pins stuck in the cloud; they begin to curve only by 3.5 s. At night at 1.5 s the ball is one sepia tone and lights the ground only as a faint brown band. The soot cloud at 3.5-7 s is good, though its lower edge hangs in vertical drips.
findings.realReference: Vehicle break-ups on film (CRS-7, Antares Orb-3, AMOS-6): for the first second a white-yellow core that clips, deep orange rolling folds edged with black soot from the start, strong contrast; fragments are bright heads on thin, kinked, quickly curving smoke threads. out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis1-launch-1.jpg: at night a fire lights its own smoke orange with dark far sides and floods the ground.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/fireball.ts: the smooth temperature field of this round has low contrast and its luminance after the flash stays under the exposure white by day; soot extinction rises too late. src/render/vfx/trail.ts: fragment trails glow for 0.03 s and are then a constant-width pale tube with no noise or drag in the first second. The fireball's light on the ground and on its own smoke is weak at night.
findings.fixDirection: Raise the fire's contrast: core above 5e5 cd/m^2 for the first third of the life so it clips, a steeper temperature-to-colour map (white, yellow, deep orange, dull red), and soot that already covers a third of the surface at 0.3 s. Give fragments ballistic curvature and drag from birth, a tapering trail with turbulent width and a head that glows for 0.3-0.5 s. At night light the smoke from inside with falling orange and make the fireball a sphere light strong enough to show the ground.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/plumes-close/staging-separation-70m.png, staging-retro-70m.png; staging/2.4s-ullage.png, 2.56s-separation.png, 2.9s-retro.png; vacuum-ignition/ignition-0.05s.png
findings.defect: The separation motors are still soft cream cones fanning out of the interstage like searchlights, smooth, symmetric and without a core, with the hull beside them washed to near white. The hydrolox ignition at 0.05 s is a soft round blue-white ball about three stage diameters across, centred on the engine plane and extending ahead of the engines. In the game (dev/a4-sep-0..2.png) the event is a soft white glow in the gap and a few specks; the retro motors are not seen at all.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/falcon9-first-stage-separation.jpg: a compact bright point with a thin expanding glow, and the spent stage's gas as a faint wisp. Saturn V S-IC / S-II staging film: eight retro jets as short, bright, straight streaks, a fast translucent shell of gas gone within half a second, and the ignition puff blown backwards past the interstage, never ahead of the engines.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json plume.solid (retro, ullage) in vacuum: a wide scattering fan without a visible core; the ignition flash (plume.hydrolox-vacuum.ignition: flash 3.5, reachRe 3-24) is an isotropic puff centred on the nozzle plane. The thruster lights wash the hull because they sit on the jet axis next to it.
findings.fixDirection: Give each small motor a bright core three to five exit diameters long and cut the fan's scatter by a stop or more; let the ignition puff travel downstream with the gas front (a half shell behind the engine plane, irregular, gone by 0.25 s); occlude the motor light by the hull. Shoot the separation in the game from the chase camera once more and make sure the retro motors show.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/dev/a4-liftoff-t1.png, a4-liftoff-t6.png; out/screens/vfx/liftoff-chase/t6-day-live.png; perf-lift-off-from-a-chase-camera-at-150-m.png (x 1840-1920 and 2010-2100, y 760-1110); splash/impact-2.5s.png
findings.defect: Low-resolution volumes sit beside full-resolution geometry and read as out of focus. In the game frames the cloud's outline is a blur several pixels wide next to a razor-sharp tower and hull, as if the smoke were on a different focal plane; four detached round blobs on the apron in a4-liftoff-t1 read as sprites. At 1440p the thin right fringe of the chase cloud is a sandy stipple rather than a fade, and two small dark wormy scribbles remain inside the sunlit cloud (liftoff-chase/t6-day, x 1020-1120, y 470-505). The splash mist is the same kind of blur.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis2-launch-2.jpg and sts97-smoke-steam-night.jpg: steam and smoke have outlines as sharp as the structures in front of them, with detail down to the pixel; thin fringes fade smoothly.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: quarter-resolution march reconstructed with a cubic B-spline over 4 x 4 rays, which is smooth but four to eight pixels wide; the fringe keeps one jitter per ray; the erosion threshold still opens small holes whose ground shadow shows dark. splash.ts mist and the pad puffs are low-detail fields or sprites.
findings.fixDirection: Add full-resolution detail where it is seen: a silhouette pass that re-evaluates the last one or two march steps (density threshold with fine noise) at full resolution for pixels whose quarter-resolution opacity lies between 0.1 and 0.9, or march at half resolution inside 300 m when the budget allows (the chase lift-off has 0.03 ms of room, so pay for it by skipping empty rays). Fade the fringe below a density floor instead of dithering it. Close holes by clamping erosion where the column behind is dense.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/close-0.4s.png, close-0.4s-live.png, close-1s.png, impact-0.4s.png, impact-1s.png
findings.defect: Splash drops read as sprites: several hundred opaque white capsules of two or three sizes, each a hard-edged pill a few pixels wide, laid over the soft crown without being lit, shadowed or occluded by it; the same pills lie in front of the capsule and behind the crown wall alike. Deterministic and live frames show the same pills in the same places.
findings.realReference: Splashdown film and out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg: spray is a continuum from sheets through ligaments to fine drops; individual drops are seen only as glints or short faint streaks, and those behind the water wall are hidden by it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/particles.ts KIND_DROPLET: drops are drawn as streaks 3.5 x their shutter path with a one-pixel minimum width and full white albedo, sorted as one transparent layer after the volume composite, so they cannot be hidden by the crown; the size range 4 mm to 9 cm collapses to the pixel minimum at this distance.
findings.fixDirection: Draw sub-pixel drops with energy-conserving coverage (alpha = true area / pixel area) so most become a faint haze and only the few large ones stay visible; attenuate each drop by the crown volume's transmittance in front of it (the moment target gives the distance); light drops with the sun's specular glint and the sky, not flat white.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/liftoff-chase/t0-day.png, t3-day.png, t6-day.png, t10-day.png; liftoff/t0-day.png, t10-day.png; engine-atlas-9m/sl-full.png against sl-full-live.png; splash/impact-5s.png against cut-away-6s.png

Chase camera by day: sky median (62,76,98), (59,72,94), (60,74,95) at T+0, 3, 6 s and (73,87,110) at T+10 s, about half a stop; pad camera (70,85,109) to (83,98,123). The same moment after splashdown is shot 1.2 EV apart depending on whether the canopies are in frame (sky 138 in impact-5s, 80 in cut-away-6s; the sea 13,53,106 against 3,20,49).
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/launch-pad/sls-pad-blue-sky.jpg and liftoff-ascent/artemis2-launch-2.jpg: a daylight sky stays at its daylight value (about 80,108,156 high up) through a launch; the steam and flame clip instead.
findings.likelyCause: The core meter (src/render/core/post/exposure.ts) still follows large bright covers within its bounds (request vfx-8 brought the lift-off step from 0.57 to 0.48 EV, with no room in the test); the live capture does not settle to the deterministic value in the engine lab; the cut-away test does not hold the exposure the splash sequence holds.
findings.fixDirection: Ask core-support for a tighter sunny-day bound (within 0.3 EV of the prior whatever transparents cover) and for one settled value in deterministic and live capture; hold the splash exposure in the cut-away shots too. Tighten the chase-sequence spec to 0.3 EV.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/engine-lyra-d/30km-min.png (x 240-330, y 355-365), engine-lyra-a/30km-min.png; engine-atlas-9m/sl-full.png, sl-min.png, 10km-min.png; engine-vela-2/30km-full.png, engine-vela-2v/30km-full.png; plumes-close/booster-45m-live.png (4x crop at the nozzles)
findings.defect: Leftovers in the liquid-engine plumes. The detached copies of round 1 are gone except for one faint lone puff a nozzle length behind the engine, after a dark gap, in the two lyra tiles at 30 km and minimum throttle. The sea-level booster flame ends in a separate island of flame. The wide fans of the hydrolox engines at 30 km show a blotchy cell pattern about 30 px across. The translucent near field between the booster nozzles and the white flame is marbled with blue and orange swirls.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/apollo6-f1-trail.jpg and falcon9-twilight-plume.jpg: a plume is one continuous body from the nozzle on, smooth where it is thin.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts: the last shock cell inside the 22-exit-radii window is still drawn where the core has faded (the lone puff); the flame's noise threshold cuts islands; the far-field noise is sampled at a single scale with too much amplitude; the near-field translucency shows the turbulence texture directly.
findings.fixDirection: Fade the cells with the core's own luminance; end the flame by luminance fall-off, not by threshold; halve the far-field noise amplitude above 20 km; drive the near field with streaks along the flow instead of isotropic noise.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/explosion/close-2.5s.png (x 270-300, y 158-186)
findings.defect: The dark bar of round 1 is still there: where the left fragment trail meets the edge of the soot cloud, two short dark vertical dashes cross the pale trail, as if a piece had been cut out of it. The trail itself is a smooth, constant-width, featureless tube.
findings.realReference: Debris trails on film are continuous turbulent threads that pass into smoke without a break.
findings.likelyCause: Not identified. The dashes sit exactly on the cloud's outline, which points to the composite of the trail (transparent pass) against the volume image: the depth-aware rejection in src/render/vfx/volumes.ts (smoothstep 1.1-1.35 of the moment distance) or the trail's own attenuation by the cloud switching within a pixel or two.
findings.fixDirection: Shoot this frame with trails, fragments and the fireball volume switched off in turn; if the trail is attenuated by the volume's moment distance, widen that transition to several pixels and filter it.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/liftoff/t10-night.png, liftoff-chase/t10-night.png, plumes-close/booster-45m-night.png; chutes/mains-full-backlit.png
findings.defect: Polish on two effects that are otherwise close. The night launch now has an orange cloud with a dark far side and a lit hull, but the flame's glare ends at its own soft edge: no halo in the air, and the vehicle above the flame at T+10 is nearly black. Full canopies are smooth and convincing from the front; against the light they are shaded like front-lit cloth and their lines almost vanish.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis1-launch-1.jpg: a wide veil of glare round the plume and warm rim light up the whole stack. out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/soyuz-ms17-chute.jpg and artemis2-mains.jpg: cloth against the sun glows through its thickness; lines are fine dark threads against a bright sky.
findings.likelyCause: Bloom is fed by a soft-edged source; the plume light does not reach the upper hull. chutes.ts applies little transmission at full inflation and lights lines independently of the view-to-sun angle.
findings.fixDirection: Add a wide, low-level glare lobe for sources above about 1e6 cd/m^2 at night and extend the plume light's reach up the hull; add single-layer transmission to the canopy and darken lines seen against a brighter background.
